what_it_does: Clo-HDnn is a chip accelerator designed for on-device machine learning that learns continuously from new data without external training. The challenge is that edge devices (phones, IoT sensors) have strict limits on power consumption and memory. Traditional neural networks require backpropagation—a mathematically intensive process that drains batteries and fills memory. Clo-HDnn instead uses hyperdimensional computing, a brain-inspired approach where each data point is encoded as a very high-dimensional vector (thousands of dimensions). The key innovation is weight clustering feature extraction: rather than processing raw pixel or sensor values, the chip first clusters (groups) them into families, drastically reducing what the learning algorithm needs to handle. Then it uses progressive search—only comparing the most relevant parts of the high-dimensional vectors instead of all of them—cutting query complexity by more than half.
